title: KPPepGen generates experimentally active pathogen-specific antimicrobial peptides
summary: KPPepGen combines Gene Ontology and pathogen-knowledge-graph prompts with a diffusion model to generate pathogen-conditioned peptide sequences. The paper reports valid peptide generation for 56 pathogens and wet-lab evaluation of nine novel peptides for Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, reporting antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity. Its Magainin 2 optimization result is a separate model-comparison metric, not a clinical outcome.

evidence.tested: The paper reports valid peptide generation for 56 pathogens and wet-lab evaluation of nine novel peptides for Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, reporting antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity.
evidence.unknown: The source reports nine experimentally evaluated peptides for E. coli and S. aureus, not experimental validation for all 56 pathogens. Antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity are in-vitro outcomes; therapeutic efficacy, safety in animals or people, and resistance outcomes are not established by this report.
evidence.ai_role: The model used pathogen-specific knowledge prompts to generate and optimize antimicrobial peptide sequences; researchers synthesized candidates and evaluated the nine reported novel peptides in wet-lab antimicrobial and cytotoxicity assays.
